headline: 10,880 runs: Smriti Mandhana becomes all-time leading run-scorer in women's cricket
summary: The Indian star smashed a spectacular 124-run century against Hong Kong, China, breaking records previously held by Mithali Raj and Meg Lanning.
details: Smriti Mandhana has etched her name in history by becoming the all-time leading run-scorer in women's international cricket. She achieved this milestone during India's victory over Hong Kong, China, at the Women's Asia Cup.

Mandhana scored a fiery 124 runs off 64 deliveries, featuring 14 fours and seven sixes. With this knock, she surpassed former India captain Mithali Raj's record of 10,868 runs, reaching a total of 10,880 runs across all formats.
The performance also saw her move past former Australian captain Meg Lanning for the most centuries in women's international cricket, marking her 18th century across formats.
India posted a total of 193/5 in 20 overs, largely driven by Mandhana's brilliance as no other Indian batter scored more than 11 runs.
In response, the Indian bowlers dominated the game. Deepti Sharma led the attack with three wickets for nine runs, while Nandani Sharma, Prema Rawat, and Shree Charani each took two wickets.
The victory puts India at the top of Group A in the Asia Cup 2026.

headline_marked: Bill placed in Parliament to [[replace RAB with SRB]]
headline: Bill placed in Parliament to replace RAB with SRB
summary: The proposed Special Security Force (SRB) would abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and take over its functions, though most of RAB's existing structure remains.
details: A bill has been placed in Parliament to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Security Force (SRB) as its replacement.
The proposed SRB Bill 2026 is expected to be reported on within four working days after a trial period.
Home Minister Asad Khan says that how the force will be operated will depend on the political will of the government.
While the SRB is intended to replace RAB, reports indicate that much of the existing structure and functions of RAB will be retained in the new force.
caption:
RAB is set to be abolished. A new bill has been placed in Parliament to replace it with the Special Security Force (SRB).

A bill has been placed in Parliament to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Security Force (SRB) as its replacement.

The proposed SRB Bill 2026 is expected to be reported on within four working days after a trial period.

Home Minister Asad Khan says that how the force will be operated will depend on the political will of the government.

While the SRB is intended to replace RAB, reports indicate that much of the existing structure and functions of RAB will be retained in the new force.
